distractors.reason: We don't say 'much late'. 'Much' goes with uncountable nouns or verbs, like 'much time' or 'much better'.
We don't say 'big late'. 'Big' describes physical size, like 'a big bus', not how late something is.
We don't say 'highly late'. 'Highly' is used with certain adjectives like 'highly important', not with 'late'.

l1_interference: Носії української мови часто перекладають 'дуже' як 'big' або 'much', тому кажуть 'much late' замість правильного 'very late'.
explanation: In English, 'very' is the most common degree adverb before everyday adjectives like 'late', 'early', 'busy' and 'full'. Use 'very' when you want to make an adjective stronger in ordinary speech.

related_collocations.example: The train was really early this morning.
The doctor is fully booked on Monday.

memory_tip: VERY = everyday strength (very late, very busy) | HIGHLY = formal strength (highly important, highly recommended)
